links.outcome: Decision-making quality (knowledge, decisional conflict) and options discussed, PERSARC vs usual care
links.effect: No significant differences in adequate knowledge (82% vs 86%) or decisional conflict (23.1 vs 18.9); treatment choices did not differ; multiple options discussed more often (93% vs 35%).
links.quote: While PERSARC did not significantly improve patients’ knowledge or decisional conflict, it led to more frequent discussion of multiple treatment options by clinicians.

unlisted_practices: Using a risk prediction model to present personalized survival estimates for treatment options to support shared decision-making

screen.reason: Cluster randomized controlled trial assessing the impact of deploying a personalized sarcoma risk prediction model (PERSARC) in clinical consultation vs usual care on patient decision quality and discussion of treatment options.
